title: EVEN and ODD: round up to pairs

steps.text: **EVEN** rounds a positive number up to the nearest even whole number: `=EVEN(number)`. Its partner `=ODD(number)` rounds up to the nearest odd whole number.

steps.prompt: Concert tickets are sold only in pairs. Select the group size in cell `A2`.
How many seats does a group of 7 need? In `B2`, type `=EVEN(A2)` and press Enter.
steps.explain: 7 is an odd number, so EVEN rounds it up to the next even number, 8.

steps.prompt: To prevent tie votes, a debate panel must have an odd number of judges. In `C2`, use ODD to round the judge count in `B2` up to an odd number.
steps.explain: 6 is an even number, so ODD rounds it up to the next odd number, 7.

steps.prompt: A workshop buys timber sold only in even whole meters. In `C2`, use EVEN to round the length in `B2` up to an even whole number.
steps.explain: EVEN rounds 2.3 up past 3 to the nearest even whole number, 4.

steps.prompt: A shuttle van seats passengers in pairs. In `C2`, use EVEN to find the seats needed for the 4 riders in `B2`.
steps.explain: 4 is already an even number, so EVEN leaves it unchanged at 4.

steps.prompt: In `C2`, use ODD to round the value in `B2` up to the next odd whole number.
steps.explain: ODD rounds 4.2 up to the next odd whole number, 5.

steps.prompt: A learner enters `=EVEN(5)` expecting 4 because 4 is also an even number close to 5. Why does Excel return 6 instead?
options: EVEN always rounds up away from zero, not to the nearest even number
EVEN rounds to whichever even number is nearest
EVEN always adds 1 to make any number even

steps.prompt: A school debate league requires each judging panel to have an odd number of judges to prevent tie votes. The finals division currently has 8 judges registered in `B2`. How many judge seats should the panel have? Put your answer in `C2`.
steps.explain: 8 is an even number, so ODD rounds it up to 9 to guarantee an odd-sized panel.
